about.title: About AI-native mini-games
about.subtitle: Short games, strong thinking.
about.whatIsNerdleText: AI-native mini-games treat AI as part of the game loop itself. In Gamelet, AI generates, evaluates, and adapts each round in real time so puzzles remain mathematically rigorous while feeling fresh for return players.
about.basicRulesText: We don't add AI as decoration. We use it inside the rule system to create dynamic scenes, valid challenge generation, and personalized pacing while keeping every outcome explainable.
about.principle1: AI creates variation without breaking game rules.
about.principle2: Every challenge keeps clear constraints that are easy to learn and verify.
about.principle3: Sessions are concise and restartable so play fits real attention spans.
about.principle4: Difficulty is adaptive to recent momentum, not random spikes.
about.principle5: Feedback is immediate and actionable, so players can improve quickly.
about.colorFeedbackText: This is not one game only; it's the design direction of Gamelet: a catalog of AI-native micro-games where novelty, fairness, and replay value reinforce each other.
about.experience2: Transparent rules and clear signal feedback
about.experience3: Easy progress from beginner to expert
about.testSkills: Open a puzzle now and feel how AI-native design changes your next decision.

tips.title: Nerdle Answer Today
tips.subtitle: Expert Strategies & Tips for Today's Puzzle
tips.whyNoAnswers: Why We Don't Provide Direct Answers
tips.whyNoAnswersText: We believe the true joy of Nerdle comes from solving the puzzle yourself. Instead of spoiling today's answer, we provide expert strategies and tips to help you develop your problem-solving skills and enjoy the satisfaction of finding the solution independently.
tips.strategy1Desc: Begin with frequently used numbers and operators like simple addition or multiplication
tips.strategy2Desc: Remember PEMDAS - equations follow standard mathematical order
tips.strategy3Desc: Use gray tiles to rule out numbers and operators not in the equation
tips.strategy4Desc: Yellow tiles tell you the element exists - try different positions
tips.strategy5Desc: Consider what makes mathematical sense given the equation length
tips.tip2: Division often results in remainders - stick to clean divisions
tips.tip3: The result must be a positive integer
tips.tip4: Don't forget about subtraction - it's less common but valid
tips.tip5: Save your guesses - think before you type
tips.useTheseStrategies: Use these expert tips to solve today's Nerdle puzzle without spoilers.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: Learn how Gamelet handles analytics, local game progress, and creative content data.
privacy.intro: Gamelet is built for lightweight play. We keep data collection narrow and use it to operate games, remember local progress, understand aggregate usage, and protect creative community features.
privacy.storageText: Puzzle progress, settings, streaks, and best scores may be stored in your browser. Grassland artwork and watering activity may be stored on our servers when you choose to publish a plant.
privacy.analyticsText: We use analytics to understand aggregate product performance. Pages may load Google services for analytics or advertising, which can process device and usage signals under their own policies.
privacy.contentText: Published plant artwork is public by design. Do not upload private, sensitive, or copyrighted material unless you have the right to share it.
privacy.contactText: For privacy questions or content removal requests, contact us through the contact page.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.description: The basic rules for playing Gamelet puzzle games and publishing creative content.
terms.intro: By using Gamelet, you agree to play fairly, respect other people's creative work, and avoid using the service in ways that damage the games or community.
terms.fairPlayText: Do not automate gameplay, abuse sharing features, attack APIs, or manipulate scoring and growth systems.
terms.contentText: You are responsible for artwork you publish. Keep uploads lawful, respectful, and appropriate for a broad audience.
terms.availabilityText: Gamelet is an evolving game platform. Features may change as we improve gameplay, safety, performance, and community tools.
terms.moderationText: We may remove content or restrict access when needed to protect users, comply with the law, or keep the games reliable.

patches.aboutText: Divide the grid into rectangles, each with exactly one clue. Numbers describe area and symbols describe shape. Every original board has one verified solution and a step-by-step logical explanation.
patches.practiceTitle: Play as much as you like.
patches.practiceText: Free practice has no daily play limit. Explore 930 practice boards and a 72-step learning path. The collection is finite: after you finish a difficulty, replay your favorites. Your progress stays in this browser.
patches.dailyText: Daily challenges use a fixed Gamelet schedule and change at midnight UTC, using your device’s date. A puzzle already in progress stays open. Gamelet challenges are separate from LinkedIn’s daily puzzle.
patches.disclosure: An independent Gamelet game with original puzzles. Not affiliated with or endorsed by LinkedIn. No account is needed; scores are personal, and hints count as assistance.
patches.difficultyDescription: Practice original {difficulty} rectangle puzzles with clear clues, undo, saved progress and step-by-step hints.

difficultyIntros.easy: Start with 5×5 grids and explicit area clues. Count the cells, compare the shape symbols and look for a rectangle that has only one possible position. These boards have a smaller initial candidate space.
difficultyIntros.medium: Move to 6×6 grids with missing area information. Use shape clues and the space left by other patches to eliminate alternatives. Every blank clue still belongs to exactly one rectangle.
difficultyIntros.hard: Take on 8×8 grids with a larger candidate space and more incomplete clues. Some deductions start at a cell rather than a clue: which legal rectangle can still cover that square?

patches.howDescription: Learn rectangle areas, shape clues, touch controls and keyboard shortcuts with original practice puzzles.
patches.strategyTitle: Patches strategy: reason through every rectangle
patches.strategyDescription: Learn to enumerate shapes, eliminate overlap and find cells with only one legal covering rectangle.

howSections.one: A 6 means exactly six cells. With a wide symbol, 3×2 and 6×1 are possible; 2×3 is tall. A square has equal sides. The diamond allows any rectangle. A dot means the area is not given.
howSections.twoTitle: 2. Draw one patch around one clue
howSections.two: Drag between opposite corners, or tap one corner and then the other. On a keyboard, use arrow keys to move and Enter or Space to choose corners. Escape cancels a selection. Every patch must contain exactly one clue, never two.
howSections.three: Patches cannot overlap, and no cell can be left empty. Tap a placed patch to remove it. Undo and redo let you explore; clearing the board can also be undone. Passing a local check does not mean a patch belongs to the final solution.
howSections.four: Open Learn & train for 12 small lessons and 60 selected practice boards. Hints first point you toward a clue, then explain a deduction, then let you place the patch. Revealing the solution records an assisted completion.

strategySections.one: Factor the area before drawing. For area 6, consider 1×6, 2×3, 3×2 and 6×1. Remove dimensions that violate the shape icon, cross a board edge or contain another clue.
strategySections.two: A completed patch removes space from neighboring clues. Revisit those neighbors before trying a distant corner. If one clue has only one legal rectangle left, that rectangle is forced.
strategySections.threeTitle: Look for a cell with only one cover
strategySections.three: A clue may have several options while an empty cell can only be reached by one of them. Since every cell must be covered, that rectangle must be chosen. Hard boards deliberately include this kind of deduction.
strategySections.four: A valid-looking rectangle can still block the unique solution. If a hint flags a conflict, remove that patch and check its neighbors. All stored explanations are verified before publication; assisted and independent results are kept distinct.
